results.title: Draft CalEnviroScreen 5.0 PM2.5 Comparison Map: With and Without Wildfire Days
results.description:
The Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment (OEHHA) announces the release of the draft CalEnviroScreen 5.0 update. CalEnviroScreen is a mapping tool that identifies California communities disproportionately burdened by pollution. This update uses the most recent census geography, incorporates the most recent data, refined methodologies, and input from community-based organizations. It also introduces two new indicators: Diabetes Prevalence and Small Air Toxic Sites.

This web app allows users to compare two methodologies for the PM2.5 indicator: the inclusion and exclusion of wildfire days from the data range. The PM2.5 indicator represents the annual average concentration of fine particulate matter, or PM2.5, in the air from 2021 to 2023. For the final draft CalEnviroScreen 5.0 results calculations, the PM2.5 indicator without wildfire days was used to better represent communities' annual PM2.5 pollution burden.

More information can be found on our Draft CalEnviroScreen 5.0 webpage. All available download data formats can be found on our Open Data Portal.
